raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

`cooperative_topk` now chooses between its single-pass and two-pass paths from each row's length instead of the
logits row stride. Rows that fit the single-pass staging no longer stream through TMA twice just because the
buffer is wide (`max_model_len`).

## Claims

- On B300, the decode top-k for rows that fit the single-pass staging is up to 8% faster when the logits stride is
  larger than the per-block staging, for example `max_model_len` 1M at 1-8 rows, or about 200K at 9-64 rows.
- Selection is unchanged: both paths compute the same exact radix top-k.
- On InferenceX AgentX, GLM-5.3 vs SGLang: together with #62170 and #62172, decode time on the same turns drops 2.0-2.9% on 4x GB200 (2.5-4.1% on 4x B300) at concurrency 1-16; by the forward benchmark this PR is about half of that.

## Validation

- `tests/kernels/test_top_k_per_row.py -k cooperative` on B300 (SM103): 73 passed, 6 skipped.
- The new `test_cooperative_topk_rows_shorter_than_stride` covers every cluster size (1, 4, 8, 33 and 64 rows) with
  strides of 64K and 1M. Its rows are 300 to 300K tokens long, so one launch mixes trivial, register, single-pass
  and streaming rows. It compares the selected values with `torch.topk`.
- Microbenchmark: `cooperative_topk`, k=2048, rows = batch x 4 (MTP), CUDA graph replay, B300:

  | rows | context | stride | before (us) | after (us) |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | 4 | 40K | 1M | 10.99 | 10.27 |
  | 4 | 40K | 64K | 10.25 | 10.16 |
  | 4 | 150K | 1M | 12.98 | 12.11 |
  | 4 | 150K | 160K | 12.21 | 12.10 |
  | 16 | 40K | 1M | 12.18 | 11.24 |
  | 16 | 40K | 256K | 12.10 | 11.18 |
  | 16 | 40K | 64K | 11.27 | 11.09 |

- Target verify forward latency (`vllm bench forward`, GLM-5.2-NVFP4, TP4, dummy weights, exact KV lengths, MTP verify shapes of B requests x 4 tokens, `max_model_len` 1M, CUDA graph; spread < 0.1%), B300, on top of #62170:

  | shape | before (us) | after (us) |
  |---|---|---|
  | 1x4 @25K | 8696.4 | 8630.6 (-0.76%) |
  | 3x4 @25K | 12231.4 | 12136.9 (-0.77%) |
  | 7x4 @25K | 17649.7 | 17547.7 (-0.58%) |
  | 1x4 @94K | 8799.6 | 8702.3 (-1.11%) |
  | 3x4 @94K | 12532.0 | 12361.1 (-1.36%) |
  | 7x4 @94K | 18116.0 | 17940.9 (-0.97%) |

- Exactness: with real MTP verification (32 GSM8K questions, greedy, one at a time), this PR stacked with the other GLM-5 top-k changes gives the same outputs (32/32) and the same acceptance length (3.4904) as main.
- End to end on B300 x4 (SM103): GLM-5.2-NVFP4, TP4, MTP 3 with synthetic acceptance length 3.0 (fixed step count), `max_model_len` 1M, FP8 KV, CUDA graphs (default sizes). Decode ms/token per request, median of 9 repetitions of (T1200 - T200) / 1000 on cached prompts (repetition spread at B=1 is about 1.5%), on top of #62170:

  | context | B | before | this PR |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | 25K | 1 | 3.171 | 3.145 (-0.8%) |
  | 94K | 1 | 3.207 | 3.190 (-0.5%) |

<details>
<summary>InferenceX AgentX setup and full results (GLM-5.3-NVFP4, vLLM vs SGLang)</summary>

InferenceX c801c9f2d AgentX scenario (pinned AIPerf), 20-minute fast mode, GLM-5.3-NVFP4 rev e3b8f9f2, TP4, MTP 3
(synthetic acceptance 2.99), native KV offload 135 GB per rank, Rust frontend, MoE autotune, `max-num-seqs` =
2 x concurrency. vLLM is main dcd07967ca with its default linear backend and default CUDA graph config, plus the
PRs cumulatively. SGLang a916d91cd3 with IMEX, TRT-LLM all-reduce fusion, `--mem-fraction-static 0.90`. Fresh
server per point, SGLang and the four vLLM variants alternating per concurrency. "Decode" is request latency minus
TTFT, summed over the turns both runs finished (a few hundred per point); fast-mode throughput alone moves about
+-2% between runs.

4x GB200 (c=1/4 on driver 580.173.02; c=8/16 on 580.178.04 after a host reinstall, SGLang rerun there too):

| decode time vs SGLang, same turns | main | + #62170, #62171, #62172 | + #62174 (flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6630, flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6631, flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6632) | + #62173 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| c=1 | +8.9% | +5.8% | +4.0% | +3.2% |
| c=4 | +12.7% | +10.6% | +7.3% | +7.3% |
| c=8 | +12.3% | +9.5% | +7.9% | +7.3% |
| c=16 | -22.6% | -25.0% | -24.5% | -24.3% |

| tok/s/GPU vs SGLang | main | + #62170, #62171, #62172 | + #62174 | + #62173 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| c=1 (SGLang 5,681) | -3.2% | -0.4% | -1.1% | +0.6% |
| c=4 (SGLang 6,783) | -0.6% | -2.4% | +0.4% | -1.7% |
| c=8 (SGLang 11,799) | -11.5% | -9.4% | -8.8% | -8.4% |
| c=16 (SGLang 10,529) | +44.7% | +45.6% | +45.8% | +46.8% |

| decode time vs the previous column, same turns | + #62170, #62171, #62172 | + #62174 | + #62173 |
|---|---|---|---|
| GB200 c=1 / c=4 / c=8 / c=16 | -2.9% / -2.0% / -2.1% / -2.9% | -1.6% / -3.1% / -1.2% / -0.4% | -0.8% / -0.9% / -0.5% / -0.1% |
| B300 c=1 / c=4 | -2.5% / -4.1% | -1.6% / -3.1% | -0.5% / -1.1% |

#62170, #62171 and #62172 were measured together; `vllm bench forward` (target verify forward, spread < 0.1%)
splits their gain about 1/6, 1/2 and 1/3.

</details>

## Details

The DSA indexer allocates its decode logits with `max_model_len` columns, and `cooperative_topk` gets that as
`stride`. The kernel sized `per_block` (elements per CTA of the cluster) from the stride. But `large_topk` splits
the row by its actual length (`seq_len`, in 16-byte units across the cluster ranks). With a long `max_model_len`,
every row took the two-pass streaming path even when its context fit the all-stages-resident single pass. For
example, 16 rows use 4-CTA clusters, and a 256K stride gives 64K elements per block, above the 48K single-pass
staging, while a 40K-token row needs only 10K per block.

`per_block` is now `ceil(seq_len / CS)`, so each row picks its path from its own length. `large_topk` rounds each
block to 16-byte units, but the single-pass limit and the stage size are multiples of that unit, so this gives the
same path and stage count as the exact split. Rows in one launch can take different paths. Each row is its own
cluster, and the barrier setup already follows the chosen path.

---

<details>
<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
</details>

files.patch:
@@ -511,9 +511,13 @@ __device__ void cooperative_topk_body(CooperativeTopKParams<TopK> params) {
     return;
   }
 
-  // Large path: init mbarriers + state, then dispatch fused or twopass
-  const uint32_t per_block =
-      (params.stride + CS - 1) / CS;  // how many elements per block
+  // Large path: init mbarriers + state, then dispatch fused or twopass.
+  // Elements per block, sized by the row's length rather than its stride so a
+  // short row in a wide logits buffer still takes the single-pass staging.
+  // large_topk splits the row in 16-byte units, but kFusedMax and
+  // kSizePerStage are multiples of that unit, so the path and stage count
+  // come out the same.
+  const uint32_t per_block = (static_cast<uint32_t>(sl) + CS - 1) / CS;
   constexpr uint32_t kFusedMax = ((CS == 16)  ? kFusedStagesCS16
                                   : (CS == 8) ? kFusedStagesCS8
                                               : kMaxSinglePassStages) *

@@ -1361,6 +1361,41 @@ def test_deepseek_topk_backends_no_error_and_reference(
     )
 
 
+@pytest.mark.skipif(not _has_device_capability(90), reason="This test requires SM90+")
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("top_k", [512, 2048])
+# 1-4 rows take the 16-CTA cluster on SM100 (8-CTA below), then 8, 4 and 2.
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("num_rows", [1, 4, 8, 33, 64])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("stride", [65536, 1048576])
+@torch.inference_mode()
+def test_cooperative_topk_rows_shorter_than_stride(
+    top_k: int, num_rows: int, stride: int
+) -> None:
+    """Each row picks its single-pass or streaming path from its own length,
+    so one launch over a wide logits buffer mixes both."""
+    torch.set_default_device("cuda:0")
+    set_random_seed(0)
+    # Trivial (<= top_k), register (<= 16384) and cluster paths, the longest
+    # rows streaming through two passes on small clusters.
+    row_lengths = [min(stride, 300000), 40000, 16384, 5000, 300]
+    lengths = [row_lengths[i % len(row_lengths)] for i in range(num_rows)]
+    logits = torch.randn(num_rows, stride)
+    workspace = torch.empty(RADIX_TOPK_WORKSPACE_SIZE, dtype=torch.uint8)
+    out = torch.empty(num_rows, top_k, dtype=torch.int32)
+    torch.ops._C.cooperative_topk(
+        logits, torch.tensor(lengths, dtype=torch.int32), out, workspace, top_k, stride
+    )
+    for row, length in enumerate(lengths):
+        k = min(top_k, length)
+        idx = out[row]
+        assert torch.all(idx[k:] == -1)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(
+            logits[row, idx[:k].long()].sort().values,
+            logits[row, :length].topk(k).values.sort().values,
+            atol=0,
+            rtol=0,
+        )
+
+
